subject: Data disposition: logs, backups & prompt lifecycle — SCCs/Evidence request
body:
From: Lena Duarte <l.duarte@veridianhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: DataPrivacy Team <dataprivacy@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Data disposition: logs, backups & prompt lifecycle — SCCs/Evidence request

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the recent walkthrough. As part of our SCCs/contracting checklist we need a concise mapping of how Redwood handles data disposition for the following categories:

- Inference request/response logs (token-level traces, model inputs/outputs)
- System/application logs (access logs, audit trails)
- Backups and disaster recovery snapshots (full/partial)
- Short-lived artifacts (KV cache, ephemeral prompt caches, streaming buffers)

Please include: default retention windows, how long items may persist in backups, whether prompts or user inputs are kept in persistent logs, legal-hold/forensic preservation behavior, and the mechanism & SLA for purge-on-request (DPA erasure requests). We also need any existing evidence: a short retention matrix and the latest SOC 2 snapshot demonstrating control mappings.

If possible, can you provide a single-file matrix and a short narrative that we can attach to our SCCs questionnaire? We are on a tight timeline for our vendor review next week.

Many thanks —
Lena
Data Privacy Manager
Veridian Health
[Attachment requested: retention_matrix.csv]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lena Duarte <l.duarte@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data disposition: logs, backups & prompt lifecycle — SCCs/Evidence request

Hi Lena, Sean,

Attached is a compact retention matrix (CSV) and a short narrative below. Ive tried to be specific to the Hosted API defaults; if you need Dedicated/Private variations we can add an extra column.

Retention summary (Hosted API default) — high level:

1) Inference logs (request/response metadata)
- Default: 30 days for request metadata (timestamps, routing, token counts).
- Model inputs/outputs: by default we do NOT persist full user prompt text in long-term logs for hosted customers unless conversation logging is enabled by the customer or if the customer opts into storage for fine-tuning/evals. When enabled, stored prompt/response pairs are retained per customer-configured retention (default 90 days).
- Backups: inference logs included in short-term backup snapshots that are retained for 90 days for operational recovery; older snapshots may exist as part of DR snapshots up to 365 days (encrypted, access-restricted).

2) System/app logs and audit trails
- Default: 90 days for searchable logs (access/audit events).
- Backups: system backups are included in rolling snapshots retained for 365 days for DR; snapshots are immutable but can be deleted earlier on a case-by-case legal/policy request.

3) Backups & snapshots
- Disaster recovery snapshots: default snapshot lifecycle is 365 days; snapshots are encrypted at rest and access-controlled (KMS).
- Customer purge on-request: For hosted customers, we can initiate targeted deletion from active indices within 48-72 hours and request snapshot purge within 7-30 days depending on replication/DR cycles. We provide a documented process and can commit to a maximum purge-on-request window of 90 days for data fully removed from backups (exceptions for forensic/legal hold).

4) Ephemeral artifacts (KV cache, streaming buffers, prompt caches)
- KV/LLM caches: short-lived in-memory and on-node caches with TTLs typically 1-7 days depending on workload; these are not persisted to long-term object storage by default.
- Streaming buffers: transient; not included in backups.

Legal hold / Forensics
- If Veridian issues a legal hold, we will preserve implicated data and pause purge workflows. Retained data under legal hold will be maintained according to the hold scope; we will provide a case-specific timeline for release.

Compliance mappings & evidence
- SOC 2: control mappings and recent snapshot are attached (SOC2-snapshot-202607.pdf). Controls around logging/retention, backup encryption, and access review are documented.
- DPA & SCCs: we support SCCs and include data-mapping fields in the DPA appendix; weve included a short DPA clause map document for quick reference (dpa_clause_map.docx).
- HIPAA/BAA: Redwood can operate under a BAA for Private deployment. For Hosted, PHI storage must be scoped and enabled per contract; we will provide the BAA template on request.

Operational notes & purge SLAs
- Erasure requests (DPR) submitted via our support portal: acknowledgement within 24 hours; targeted deletion from live indices within 48-72 hours; snapshot purge initiated and completed within 7-30 days where possible; full removal from all redundant backups targeted within 90 days.
- Exceptions: forensic holds, regulatory obligations, or subpoena/Litigation holds may delay purge. We log all deletion actions and can provide an audit trail.

Attachments included:
- retention_matrix.csv (per-data-type rows, retention windows, backup windows, purge SLA)
- SOC2-snapshot-202607.pdf (control snapshot)
- dpa_clause_map.docx (quick DPA clause references)

If youd like, Marissa and I can produce a one-page attestation table with exact DPA clause pointers and the purge-on-request timeline called out for inclusion in your SCCs questionnaire.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
